description:
We represent Umay Aerospace from Özdemir Bayraktar Aviation and Space Technology High School (ÖBHUT MTAL), competing as a dedicated two-person engineering team in NASA Space Apps.

With our background in aviation and space technologies, we bring an engineering-first mindset to real-world challenges. Together, we cover system architecture, algorithmic logic, and NASA data analysis to build a realistic, technically grounded, and high-impact project
summary:
Fire Calendar is an open web and Windows application that merges NASA's two active-fire records, MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20/21), into one continuous and comparable fire history for any region on Earth.

The two sensors see fire differently: VIIRS detects many more small fires, so simply joining the records creates false upward trends. MODIS is also nearing the end of its mission. Our method puts both FIRMS datasets on a common 0.25° cell-day grid and removes static heat sources such as industry and gas flares. It then learns a region-specific transfer curve from the years when both sensors observed together. The curve is tested on years it was not trained on, and orbital-drift years are reported separately. Every harmonized value comes with an uncertainty estimate and a confidence label.

Users pick a region on a globe or flat map and get a fire calendar, sensor comparisons, satellite overpass times and a downloadable report.

Long, consistent fire records are essential for tracking climate-driven changes in fire seasons, for planning fire management, and for keeping two decades of NASA observations useful after MODIS ends.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Fire Calendar turns NASA's two active-fire records, MODIS (Terra/Aqua, since 2000) and VIIRS (S-NPP since 2012, NOAA-20/21), into one consistent fire history. The user picks any region on an interactive globe or flat map, and the app:

1. Downloads or loads FIRMS hot spots for both sensors and places them on a common 0.25° cell-day grid.

2. Removes static heat sources (industry, gas flares, volcanoes) that would otherwise be counted as fires every day.

3. Learns a region-specific transfer curve: for each level of MODIS activity, how much VIIRS activity is expected. It uses only years when both sensors observed together. The curve is binned and forced to be monotonic so it stays physically sensible.

4. Validates the curve with a temporal split: trained on early years, tested on later years it has never seen. Years affected by Terra/Aqua orbital drift are reported separately.

5. Shows the result as a day-by-day fire calendar, side-by-side sensor comparisons, satellite overpass times, an uncertainty band and a confidence label for every region. A report can be downloaded.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Simply joining the two records creates fake trends, because VIIRS detects many more small fires. Our harmonization lets researchers, forest services and disaster agencies compare 2005 with 2025 fairly. It also keeps two decades of MODIS observations useful after the MODIS mission ends. Because every region gets its own curve and an honest confidence label, users know where the harmonized record can be trusted and where it cannot.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

- Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1, VIIRS S-NPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21)

- Analysis: Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, requests)

- Interface: HTML, CSS, JavaScript; OpenStreetMap tiles and Nominatim search

- Web version: GitHub Pages. All calculations run in the visitor's browser from compressed binary data tiles, with no server.

- Desktop version: a Windows app packaged with PyInstaller that works fully offline

- Hardware: standard laptops only

- Bilingual interface (Turkish/English)

CREATIVITY

- Instead of one global correction factor, every region gets its own learned curve, because fire behaviour in Siberia, the Amazon and Anatolia is very different.

- The "fire calendar" view shows decades of fire seasons at a glance, with both sensors on the same scale.

- The app tells users when not to trust a result, using uncertainty and confidence labels, instead of hiding weak fits.

- The full analysis engine runs in a web browser, so anyone can use it for free from a single link.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Different sensor resolution (1 km vs 375 m) and detection sensitivity

- Overpass times: Terra morning, Aqua and VIIRS early afternoon

- Orbital drift of Terra and Aqua, and the transition from S-NPP to NOAA-20/21

- Static heat sources that are not wildfires

- Overfitting, avoided by testing only on unseen years

- Accessibility: free hosting, offline desktop version, no API key needed for the ready-made world data

- Privacy and security: personal API keys stay on the user's computer and are never uploaded
